finding.claim: The DELETE handler calls the async authorize() without await. The 403 is thrown inside a promise that is never awaited, so the handler goes on to delete the report anyway. Any authenticated user can delete any report. The rejected promise also becomes an unhandled rejection, which can crash the process on Node 15+.
finding.source: Any authenticated user sends DELETE /reports/:id with an arbitrary report id.

trace.note: The report is loaded by the attacker-supplied id.
authorize() returns a promise that is not awaited, so the rejection is not observed and execution continues.
The grants lookup and the 403 throw happen asynchronously, after the handler has already moved on.
The report is removed regardless of the authorization result.

finding.guards_checked: authorize() itself is correct, and the PUT handler awaits it at line 27. The DELETE handler is the only call site that does not await it. No other middleware does authorization. Express 4 does not catch async errors, so there is no global error handler to stop the delete.

verdict.guard_found: authorize() at server.js:9-16 throws 403 correctly, but the DELETE handler's call at line 20 is not awaited. No other authorization middleware exists (lines 4-7 only set req.user), and there is no error handler.
verdict.reason: server.js:20 calls async authorize() without await, so the 403 thrown at server.js:14 is never observed and db.reports.remove runs at server.js:21; the PUT handler at server.js:27 awaits it, which shows the intended pattern.

finding.claim: The middleware reads req.session.user, but no session middleware is installed. req.session is undefined, so every request throws a TypeError and the server returns 500. If a session were added without an authentication check, req.user could be undefined. Handlers would then crash at user.id in authorize(), and there is no check that the user is logged in. This is a missing-authentication and robustness flaw, not a directly exploitable bypass.
finding.sink: req.user = req.session.user at server.js:5, and user.id at server.js:10.

trace.note: Only express.json() is registered, with no session or auth middleware.
req.session is dereferenced without being defined.
authorize() dereferences user.id with no null check.

finding.guards_checked: No authentication guard, session setup or null check was found in this file. The repository contains only server.js, so session setup elsewhere cannot be confirmed.

verdict.guard_found: No session or auth middleware exists in server.js. The only effective control is a fail-closed crash. server.js:5 throws a TypeError when req.session is undefined, and Express returns 500 before any handler runs. server.js:10 would also throw if user were undefined. At server.js:27 authorize() is awaited, so a failure stops the PUT.
verdict.reason: The trace is accurate (server.js:3, 5, 10), but the claimed failure is fail-closed: the TypeError at server.js:5 blocks every request before any handler runs, and if a session were added without a login check, an undefined user would still throw at server.js:10 and stop the awaited PUT at server.js:27. No unauthenticated request can reach an effect, and the finding itself concedes it is not an exploitable bypass. A separate real bug exists at server.js:20, where authorize() is not awaited in the DELETE handler, so the delete at server.js:21 runs even when authorization fails.

finding.claim: The PUT handler passes the whole request body to db.reports.update(). A user with write access can overwrite any field on the report, including owner, id or ACL fields (mass assignment). The impact depends on the db schema, which is not in this repository.
finding.source: The JSON body of PUT /reports/:id from a user who holds the write grant.

trace.note: The authorize check only verifies the write grant.
req.body is passed to the update unfiltered.

finding.guards_checked: There is no field allowlist or schema validation. The db layer is not present, so any filtering inside db.reports.update cannot be ruled out.

verdict.guard_found: authorize() at server.js:9-16 (awaited at :27, throws 403 on missing write grant); no field allowlist or schema validation in the handler
verdict.reason: server.js:28 passes req.body unfiltered to db.reports.update after the awaited write-grant check at :27, but whether owner/id/ACL fields are overwritable depends on the db layer, which is not in this repo.
